transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (CTO - Spearhead), Priya Mehta (Head of ML), Hannah Lee (Platform)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Liam our SE. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Jamal Ortiz: good, thanks. busy, but excited to dig in.
[00:12] Maya Chen: cool. quick agenda — we want to understand your latency/throughput targets, concurrency, streaming needs, and then propose a bench/pilot plan. sound ok?
[00:22] Priya Mehta: yes, high level — we have two main flows: auth & routing (short prompts, low latency required) and agent-style chat for customer support (longer streaming responses). p95 for auth must be under 200ms ideally, but willing to consider up to 300ms if cost is prohibitive.
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: ok that's helpful. when you say p95 200ms are you measuring end-to-end from your app or token-generation time? often the big number is model token generation.
[00:50] Priya Mehta: it's end-to-end so including network and our proxy, but we've isolated model time in previous tests — we're trying to understand where Redwood can help with variance and batching.
[01:04] Hannah Lee: and on concurrency, our peak is about 1.2k concurrent requests during batch windows, but steady state concurrent for auth is ~200 qps. for chat agents concurrency per user is 4 to 8, but overall chat concurrency about 300.
[01:22] Jamal Ortiz: also want streaming — the chat UI expects token-by-token streaming with first token within ~250ms. If first token is delayed that's a poor user experience.
[01:34] Liam O'Connor: got it. couple clarifying q's — what model families are you evaluating, and do you have a preference for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[01:44] Priya Mehta: we're testing open models (Mistral-style and Llama-derivatives), and evaluating Anthropic for safety. Cost is a big factor so we'd like hosted first; but dedicated if we need guaranteed throughput / lower jitter, and private only if compliance requires.
[02:00] Maya Chen: makes sense — common pattern. for hosted we typically present validated perf profiles. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more predictable p95 and less noisy neighbors. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict residency or air-gapped needs.
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: on benchmarks — what we'd propose is a two-tier benchmark: 1) latency microbench (single-request p95 for prompt lengths you care about) across model variants and quantization profiles, including token/sec and first-token latency; 2) throughput run with concurrency matrix (e.g., 50, 200, 500, 1k, 1.2k) measuring p95 and tokens/sec sustained over 10–60 minutes per scenario.
[02:40] Priya Mehta: that sounds good. curious about batching — we are concerned that automatic batching can hurt p95 for auth flows. we need predictable tail latency.
[02:51] Liam O'Connor: understood. Redwood supports fine-grained routing: you can route latency-sensitive calls to low-batch, low-latency instances and background or bulk traffic to high-batch optimized instances. we also provide KV/prefix caching to speed up repeated contexts and reduce token work.
[03:08] Jamal Ortiz: any numbers you can share for p95 at various concurrency on your hosted offering? ballpark is fine.
[03:14] Maya Chen: ballpark on hosted with optimized open models: for short prompts (20–40 tokens model-side), p95 first-token around 120–180ms in best cases; end-to-end often adds 40–80ms depending on region and proxy. under heavy concurrency p95 can move up, which is where dedicated helps — dedicated can hold p95 growth to ~1.5x of baseline based on similar customers.
[03:38] Priya Mehta: interesting. we need to be careful about how you measure p95 — do you include our app layer?
[03:43] Liam O'Connor: our bench will report model-generation latency and end-to-end if you can deploy a small agent in your environment or share a proxy. otherwise we'll simulate typical network RTTs.
[03:55] Hannah Lee: we run in AWS us-east-1 mostly, with some eu-west for redundancy. we care about regional variance.
[04:03] Liam O'Connor: fine. we'll run region-specific benches. question on streaming: are you okay with chunked tokens or do you need one-token-at-a-time flushes?
[04:14] Jamal Ortiz: chunked is fine as long as first chunk arrives quickly. developer UX wants sub-250ms to first chunk in 95% cases.
[04:23] Priya Mehta: on traffic profile: our auth prompts are very short — 10–30 tokens output, chat average 100–350 tokens. During peak we see many short auth calls mixed with chat. that mixed workload is tough.
[04:38] Liam O'Connor: that's a classic mixed workload. Redwood can set two routes: low-latency route with small-batch/low-queueing for auth, and high-throughput route for chat. routing policies can be by route key or header. we can also do fallback policies if a dedicated pool is fully used.
[04:54] Jamal Ortiz: about quantization — we have questions about quality impact vs speed — have you seen quality regressions with int8 or int4 for our workloads?
[05:03] Liam O'Connor: minimal in many cases for open models, but it depends on model and evals. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload. we can include a quality-regression check in the bench using your eval prompts.
[05:16] Priya Mehta: perfect. what about KV cache hits — can that drastically reduce tokens/sec?
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: yes, prefix/KV caching is high impact for repeated contexts. for example, for chat with long system prompts we can avoid re-sending tokens and speed up generation. we'll instrument cache hit rates in the bench.
[05:33] Maya Chen: next — security/compliance: you mentioned SOC2, KMS, and audit logs in your RFP. any additional must-haves?
[05:41] Jamal Ortiz: we need KMS integration for key separation, SSO with SAML, RBAC, and detailed audit trails. also, data retention opt-out for certain flows.
[05:54] Maya Chen: Redwood supports all those; we'll include SOC2 whitepaper + KMS integration doc in the pack.
[05:59] Hannah Lee: on cost: can you give a sense of delta between hosted vs dedicated? we assume dedicated is more expensive but more predictable.
[06:08] Maya Chen: correct — hosted is usage-based and often lower for spiky, low-volume workloads. dedicated is commit-based with lower per-token cost at scale and importantly predictable tail latency. we'll share an example TCO calc as part of pricing.
[06:21] Priya Mehta: ok, let's align on bench scope and success criteria. our primary success metric: p95 end-to-end for auth under 300ms across region, and first-token p95 for streaming under 250ms. secondary: sustain 15k tokens/sec aggregate during peak with p95 under our threshold for chat.
[06:41] Liam O'Connor: that gives us concrete targets. we'll propose a bench that includes: single-request p95 matrix (prompt lengths: 20, 100, 300 tokens); concurrency sweep (50, 200, 500, 1k, 1.2k); streaming-first-token checks; and a 60-minute sustained throughput run at peak concurrency.
[07:00] Jamal Ortiz: timeline — can we run this next week? we can provide sample prompts and an envoy proxy to measure end-to-end.
[07:07] Maya Chen: yes — if you share prompts by Friday (2026-06-05) and provide test creds or proxy details, we can schedule bench for week of 06/08.
[07:17] Priya Mehta: sounds good. a couple of practical items: how do you handle cold-starts / model load times for dedicated?
[07:24] Liam O'Connor: dedicated pools keep models resident; cold-starts are rare unless you swap model variants. hosted may evict based on usage, but we can pin models with warm-up policies. we'll include expected cold-start metrics in the bench report.
[07:38] Hannah Lee: any limitations on token/sec when using streaming + low-latency route?
[07:43] Liam O'Connor: there is a tradeoff — ultra-low latency routes avoid heavy batching which reduces tokens/sec efficiency. That's why we separate routes. for chat throughput we use batch-optimized hardware and quantization to hit high tokens/sec.
[07:57] Maya Chen: ok let's recap and assign action items.
[08:01] Maya Chen: action: I'll send pricing, SOC2, and security pack by 06/04.
[08:06] Liam O'Connor: action: I'll draft the benchmark plan with concurrency matrix and stream tests, include region variance and caching instrumentation by 06/07.
[08:13] Priya Mehta: action: we'll share sample prompt set, p95 targets, and a small traffic trace by 06/05.
[08:20] Jamal Ortiz: we'll also identify a staging environment and provide a short-lived proxy token for end-to-end measurement.
[08:27] Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[08:30] Jamal Ortiz: nope that's it for now. thanks.
[08:33] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and the bench plan.
[08:37] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: a few words may be off (model names & acronyms), timestamps are approximate.
